The team also found greater bile acid modification in the mice.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To determine patterns in humans, they reanalysed publicly available data from a human ageing cohort, analysing bile acid measurements from 48 young adults, 107 older adults and 125 centenarians.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — किसी भी अदालत ने अभी तक यह नहीं पूछा है कि क्या राज्य किसी नागरिक की बांझपन देखभाल तक पहुंच पूरी तरह से उनके अपने खर्च पर छोड़ सकता है।।

1. Core Context & Background: Indian laws protect the decision not to have a child through statutes, schemes and subsidies, but the decision to have one is left to the mercy of the private assisted reproduction healthcare market

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The reproductive-autonomy jurisprudence as evolved by the Supreme Court under Article 21 of the Constitution is rich yet narrow, focusing primarily on one side of the problem. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department (2022), the Supreme Court extended the right to abortion to unmarried women as an exercise of ‘decisional autonomy’.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These, and nearly all other landmark cases are concerned only with an existing pregnancy. The freedom to pursue parenthood through medical treatment, however, has surfaced only at the margins. The Delhi High Court, in 2023, allowed parole of a life convict to attempt IVF, by recognising a “right to parenthood,” but only as a claim against a barrier the State itself had erected. No court has yet asked whether the State may leave a citizen’s access to infertility care entirely to their own purse. articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days. On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri. Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year . When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay. “El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas. And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ramakrishna also pointed out that in October and November, the Bay of Bengal consistently retained high sea surface temperatures—over 26.5 degrees Celsius—and anything above 26 is conducive to developing a cyclonic system. 1. Core Context & Background: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh is currently facing a rare weather phenomenon. Since October 28, the State has already been hit by two back-to-back cyclonic storms, and there is an imminent threat of another one battering the coastal districts in the next two days. On October 28, the State was battered by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab , which made landfall near Narsapur in West Godavari district. On November 3, it was hit again by severe cyclonic storm Murasu , which made landfall close to Ongole in Prakasam district. Now, cyclonic storm Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and make landfall on November 20 between Narsapur and Puri. Three tropical storms battering the coast within less than a month during the post-monsoon season is a rare scenario. The last times such a thing happened were in 1976, 1987 and 2013. Both 1976 and 1987 were El Niño years, and this year is also categorised as a super El Niño year . When it comes to tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal, there are a number of driving factors, and El Niño is just one of them. Mostly, the formation of storms over the Bay, especially their frequency and intensity, differs slightly from the rest of the world, because the Bay of Bengal is almost a land-locked sea, said S.S.V.S. Ramakrishna, former head of the Department of Oceanography and Meteorology, Andhra University, who has spent over four decades researching the pattern of cyclones over the Bay. “El Niño typically suppresses the southwest summer monsoon over India, but it has the opposite effect on the Northeast (winter) Monsoon and post-monsoon cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal,” he said. El Niño drought then floods hit North Andhra farmers El Niño, a deficient monsoon, and the heat to come During El Niño years, the northeast monsoon tends to be significantly more active over southern peninsular India. This creates continuous moisture convergence and frequent convective disturbances over the southern Bay, providing a steady assembly line of low-pressure areas. And sometimes, in rare occurrences, remnants of a Pacific Ocean cyclone cross the Strait of Malacca, re-enter the Bay of Bengal, and intensify into a cyclone. “We had seen this phenomenon during the Odisha Super Cyclone in 1999,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ramakrishna also pointed out that in October and November, the Bay of Bengal consistently retained high sea surface temperatures—over 26.5 degrees Celsius—and anything above 26 is conducive to developing a cyclonic system. This has been aided by the El Niño-modified upper-level wind patterns over the southern Bay of Bengal, which reduce vertical wind shear.

articles.title: Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Demand for air purifiers in India has witnessed explosive growth in 2026, with major brands and retail platforms reporting sales doubling or tripling year-on-year. Driven by an early surge ahead of the traditional winter pollution season , consumer behaviour is shifting toward viewing indoor air quality as a year-round health priority rather than an emergency seasonal purchase. According to industry leaders, adoption is gaining momentum well before peak pollution months. Smart tech brand Qubo recorded a 150 percent growth over the previous year, while Xiaomi registered approximately 3X year-on-year sales growth during the festive period. Industry executives note that growing awareness surrounding indoor pollutants, ranging from dust and pet dander to everyday cooking and cleaning emissions, is encouraging households to take a proactive approach to home wellness throughout the year. Retail footprint and online traffic reflect this expanding market footprint across the country. Electronics retailer Croma reported that air purifier sales volumes have more than doubled in 2026. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks. Premium tech maker Dyson also reported that visits to its air purifier pages grew by over 100 percent in October compared to the same period last year. Modern buyers are increasingly seeking advanced functionality and intelligent filtration tech. Croma highlighted strong consumer interest in models featuring real-time AQI displays, app controls, and multi-functional units combining purification with humidification or heating. On e-commerce platforms, Amazon India reported that sales doubled over the past week. Shoppers are actively leveraging Rufus, Amazon’s personalised AI shopping assistant, to filter models by room size, filter type, and live sensor capabilities, prompting the e-retailer to expand selection on Amazon Now for immediate delivery. “We have observed a notable increase in consumer demand for air purifiers on Flipkart, reflected in higher search activity, product discovery and purchases. Northern India continues to account for a significant share of demand for the category. We also witnessed a rise in purchases during the early hours following Diwali, coinciding with heightened concerns around deteriorating air quality and the steps households are taking to manage their indoor environments,” said Flipkart.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: technology (general) / gadgets (general) / accessories

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 05:23:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Demand for air purifiers in India has witnessed explosive growth in 2026, with major brands and retail platforms reporting sales doubling or tripling year-on-year. Driven by an early surge ahead of the traditional winter pollution season , consumer behaviour is shifting toward viewing indoor air quality as a year-round health priority rather than an emergency seasonal purchase. According to industry leaders, adoption is gaining momentum well before peak pollution months. Smart tech brand Qubo recorded a 150 percent growth over the previous year, while Xiaomi registered approximately 3X year-on-year sales growth during the festive period. Industry executives note that growing awareness surrounding indoor pollutants, ranging from dust and pet dander to everyday cooking and cleaning emissions, is encouraging households to take a proactive approach to home wellness throughout the year. Retail footprint and online traffic reflect this expanding market footprint across the country. Electronics retailer Croma reported that air purifier sales volumes have more than doubled in 2026. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks. Premium tech maker Dyson also reported that visits to its air purifier pages grew by over 100 percent in October compared to the same period last year. Modern buyers are increasingly seeking advanced functionality and intelligent filtration tech. Croma highlighted strong consumer interest in models featuring real-time AQI displays, app controls, and multi-functional units combining purification with humidification or heating. On e-commerce platforms, Amazon India reported that sales doubled over the past week. Shoppers are actively leveraging Rufus, Amazon’s personalised AI shopping assistant, to filter models by room size, filter type, and live sensor capabilities, prompting the e-retailer to expand selection on Amazon Now for immediate delivery. “We have observed a notable increase in consumer demand for air purifiers on Flipkart, reflected in higher search activity, product discovery and purchases. Northern India continues to account for a significant share of demand for the category. We also witnessed a rise in purchases during the early hours following Diwali, coinciding with heightened concerns around deteriorating air quality and the steps households are taking to manage their indoor environments,” said Flipkart.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: technology (general) / gadgets (general) / accessories

✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
Humidification (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Humidification' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart featur' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart fea' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart fea' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks." (Hinglish Arth: जबकि दिल्ली-एनसीआर प्रमुख बाजार बना हुआ है, मुंबई जैसे शहर और पारंपरिक उच्च प्रदूषण बेल्ट से परे क्षेत्र निरंतर वृद्धि दिखा रहे हैं)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. technology (general) / gadgets (general) / accessories.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "technology (general) / gadgets (general) / accessories." (Hinglish Arth: प्रौद्योगिकी (सामान्य) / गैजेट (सामान्य) / सहायक उपकरण)

articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole. A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Text and Context / economy / Artificial Intelligence / labour

📰 How AI could reshape global growth and productivity

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:54:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole. A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Text and Context / economy / Artificial Intelligence / labour

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.

1. Core Context & Background: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war. Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: prison / judiciary (system of justice) / crime, law and justice / United Nations / death penalty policies

1. Core Context & Background: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

1. Core Context & Background: India should use multilateral fora to advance bilateral cooperation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Students of Classes VII and IX of the Coimbatore Public School have developed a fruit harvesting toolkit for coffee cherries. On Thursday, their innovation, for which they have applied for a patent on June 25, 2026, was passed on to a start-up firm for commercialisation. The toolkit has a hollow pipe attached to a harvesting head that has a set of blades to cut off the ripe coffee cherries. The set of blades arranged in V-shape are guided by a push-pull casting while harvesting. The picked cherries glide through the hollow flexible hose into a storage container. The purpose of the innovation was to increase the efficiency and speed of fruit harvesting operations in plantations. This was one of the 10 products for which technology transfer took place at the Tamil Nadu Technology Transfer Summit 2006, organised jointly by the Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology (TNSCST) and Anna University. S.A. Nirmala, correspondent, Coimbatore Public School, said that every year, the students work on a real-life problem that is brought in either by parents or the community. This prototype was the product of one such problem brought in by a parent. The technology was transferred to Nexorasai Pvt. Ltd., a startup firm started by the parent. Before the handover, students tested the prototype at a coffee plantation for efficacy, she said. Among the new innovations are a drone-based infrastructure cleaning system developed by Anna University, a sanitary napkin vending machine developed by VIT Chennai, foxtail millet cookies technology, millet muesli, banana stem juice, and low-fat dessicated coconut chips technology. S. Vincent, member secretary, TNSCST, said a total of 97 innovative technologies had emerged from higher education institutions in the State which were ready to be transferred for commercialisation. While only 10 technologies were transferred to start-ups and MSMEs for commercialisation, at least 60 industry representatives had participated at the Summit and had shown interest in the innovations. Inaugurating the Summit, P. Viswanathan, Higher Education Minister, said it would be made into an annual affair and would be taken to other major cities in Tamil Nadu as well. He released a book titled A Compendium of Registered Geographical Indications of Tamil Nadu documenting the State’s heritage of traditional products and indigenous knowledge. Researchers at IIT-Madras have developed a software to help identify items for probable GI registration and also address post-GI challenges such as marketing of the produce and maintaining its authenticity. Utthan India, a non-governmental organisation, working with tribal communities across India, will provide scientific and technological intervention to address problems faced by these communities. The TNSCST signed memoranda of understanding with the two institutions. Another MoU with Asian Research Association envisages training programmes for students in the State to write scientific papers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Dheeraj Kumar, Higher Education Secretary, V. Kumaresan, Registrar-in-charge, Anna University, and A. Ramanan, Scientific Officer, TNSCST, also spoke.

Chandrasekhar said medical education must keep pace with technological advancements and changing healthcare needs. He said medical institutions should take advantage of the opportunities emerging from the State’s technology initiatives by working closely with engineering colleges, research organisations and industry. The initiative is envisaged as part of the emerging innovation ecosystem associated with Amaravati Quantum Valley and Bio Valley. It would focus on identifying real-world healthcare problems and developing solutions through biomedical design, engineering and technology, the participants discussed. The school has been proposed at the Vivenns campus in Mayuri Tech Park, Mangalagiri, with its inauguration planned for December 7, 2026.

Gales of 90 kmph to 100 kmph are also likely along the coast in North Coastal Andhra Pradesh around the midnight. Already, strong winds of 50 kmph to 60 kmph are prevailing along the coast, the Director said. Parvathipuram-Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli districts may also record isolated very heavy rainfall till Friday evening, but the rest of the State may not see any rainfall activity on Friday. Weather experts said while the weather system may move closer to the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha, which is around 180 km from Srikakulam, there is a slight possibility of the system making landfall near the extreme end of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh as well. Meanwhile, as per the latest bulletin issued by the IMD at 5.30 p.m., Akvan moved northwards with the speed of 13 kmph till 2.30 p.m. and remained over the west-central Bay of Bengal, which is about 390 km east-southeast of Narsapur and 320 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam of Andhra Pradesh, 410 km south of Gopalpur and 470 km south of Puri of Odisha and 610 km east-northeast of Chennai of Tamil Nadu. It is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross the coast close to Gopalpur by Friday noon, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90kmph to 100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A storm surge of 0.5 to 1.0 metre height above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas along the coastal belt in the districts of Kakinada, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam districts, the IMD said in its bulletin.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: He announces that Anna University has been asked to take the lead in developing this digital platform

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department will soon be starting a central digital repository of all research and innovation that are taking place in higher education institutions in the State, Higher Education Secretary Dheeraj Kumar said on Thursday. Speaking at the Tamil Nadu Technology Transfer Summit 2026 organised jointly by the Tamil Nadu State Council for Science and Technology (TNSCST) and Anna University, Mr. Kumar said the repository would serve as a platform that would link various universities and institutions carrying out research and innovation in various fields, the industry, and the governmental and non-governmental organisations working with the innovators. Later, elaborating on the initiative, he told The Hindu , “Development of technology generally gets spurred by a problem statement. Instead of doing the research ab initio , it is possible that some research would have already happened in certain universities of our State or some research institutions or centres that will be relevant to the solution that is now being sought. The point is to connect them.” Mr. Kumar said Anna University had been asked to take the lead in developing the digital platform. “They have three incubation centres. We thought of looking at the domains that are industry-oriented that can be pushed first,” he added. The initiative will entail the creation of a portal where all research work being carried out in universities and research institutions and innovative pursuits at incubation centres would be catalogued and put up. It will act as a common interface for stakeholders involved in the State’s innovation journey, from incubation to commercialisation, said V. Kumaresan, Registrar-in-charge, Anna University.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Explaining further, he said if a business house or a start-up firm is looking for a specific technology or process, instead of running from pillar to post they could visit the portal and tap into the research work being carried out by institutions across the State. “It will help the State to identify areas where we are s t rong, research areas where the universities are working, and the possible avenues for innovation,” Dr. Kumaresan added.
